我将采用演示方案中的公开先验：**405 kyr 建立相对时间轴；210 Ma 仅用于轨道目标近似；19 次模拟用于快速探索**。以下所有数值与图件均由 MATLAB/Acycle 原始例程计算。

## 数据与血缘

| 环节 | 运行 ID | 输入哈希 | 实际结果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 导入 | — | `1cd82c19…b65ac2` ✔ 与 manifest 一致 | 39,218 B，CR 换行，2 344 行，`depth_m`／`depth_rank` |
| Interpolation Pro | `20261025T105410Z-2d857a4092b0` | `625d94a0…` | linear，dt=0.85344 m；**0 间隙、0 重者、无外推**；2 344→2 344，0–1999.60992 m |
| 深度谱／EvoFFT／滤波 | `20261025T105716Z-dbf6eaaeabb0` | 同上 | lowess 0.35，NW=2，600 m 窗／50.35 m 步；Gaussian 48–80 m 带通 |
| COCO | `20261025T105950Z-0531b1ec894c` | 同上 | 21 个速率（5–25 cm/kyr），210 Ma 九目标 |
| eCOCO | `20261025T110220Z-a5880602e02b` | 同上 | 14 完整窗（600 m／100 m），无边缘填充 |
| 定年（峰） | `20261025T110455Z-2b96156ba364` | `1b97d448…` | 35 控制点，6.83–1944.99 m → 0–13 770 kyr |
| 时间诊断（峰） | `20261025T110726Z-6e76718b431c` | `1cd82c19…`（原始） | 2272 行入模，5 kyr 网格 |
| 定年（谷，相位检验） | `20261025T111033Z-221e2d5fa8d7` | 同滤波文件 | 35 控制点，30.72–1972.30 m |
| 时间诊断（谷） | `20261025T111312Z-bc14efa3b318` | `1cd82c19…` | 同上参数 |

## 四个主要观察

**1. 深度中存在持续的 ~60 m 节律。** MTM 前三峰 57.16 m、61.36 m、53.78 m（稳健 AR(1) ρ=0.43，点态均超 95%），另有 270/238 m 的低频能量。谱峰落在预先声明的 48–80 m 带内而**不在其中心**，说明它并非纯粹由选带造成；但选带来自 Kent & Olsen (1999) 的区域先验，仍属探索性候选。

**2. 速率搜索没有得到统计支持。** COCO 最佳 7 cm/kyr（Spearman ρ=0.378），但 **21 个速率的 rate-global p 全部 ≥0.95**；19 个 AR(1) 替代序列的最大相关为 0.369–0.450，观测值正落在其中间。7 cm/kyr 处仅 **6/9** 个目标周期可分辨（全九周期解需 ≥9.66 cm/kyr）。eCOCO 逐窗 global p 最低 0.05（仅 600–900 m），1200–1500 m 全部为 1，且不跨窗校正。**因此短偏心率检验未获证实**；19 次模拟本身也不可能达到 p<0.05。

**3. 沿剖面速率并非常数。** eCOCO 追踪速率自 300 m 的 6 cm/kyr 单调升至 1600 m 的 13 cm/kyr（294 个有限格点，0 个未解点）；定年隐含的 35 段速率为 7.6–17.1 cm/kyr。两条独立途径在"变速率"上一致，但绝对值系统性偏差约一倍。

**4. 循环计数对相位选择稳健。** 峰分支与谷分支各自独立选出 **35 个极值**，均覆盖 0–13 770 kyr。这是本方案中最实质的可靠性证据——计数不依赖"峰或谷"约定。

## 图件

深度 MTM 谱与 EvoFFT（`20261025T105716Z-dbf6eaaeabb0`）：

![20261025T105716Z-dbf6eaaeabb0: spectrum_png](</workspace/harness-conversation-runs/v05-newark-fixedtransport/.acycle/runs/20261025T105716Z-dbf6eaaeabb0/outputs/spectrum.png>)
*稳健 AR(1) 95% 为点态阈值；57–61 m 峰簇超出，但点态检验不控制多重比较。*

![20261025T105716Z-dbf6eaaeabb0: evolution_png](</workspace/harness-conversation-runs/v05-newark-fixedtransport/.acycle/runs/20261025T105716Z-dbf6eaaeabb0/outputs/evolution.png>)
*0.016–0.019 cyc/m 带在整个剖面间断续出现；两端为补零窗，边缘约束较弱。*

COCO 速率诊断（`20261025T105950Z-0531b1ec894c`）：

![20261025T105950Z-0531b1ec894c: coco_figure_1_png](</workspace/harness-conversation-runs/v05-newark-fixedtransport/.acycle/runs/20261025T105950Z-0531b1ec894c/outputs/coco_figure_1.png>)
*相关性随速率起伏平缓，无单一锐利极值——与全局 p≈1 一致。*

eCOCO 图（`20261025T110220Z-a5880602e02b`）：

![20261025T110220Z-a5880602e02b: ecoco_figure_1_png](</workspace/harness-conversation-runs/v05-newark-fixedtransport/.acycle/runs/20261025T110220Z-a5880602e02b/outputs/ecoco_figure_1.png>)
*B 面板（global p）除 600–800 m／6–8 cm/kyr 局部浅色外几乎全为深蓝（p≈1）；D 面板显示 <10 cm/kyr 处仅 4–8 个周期可分辨。*

滤波曲线与 405 kyr 控制点（`20261025T110455Z-2b96156ba364`）：

![20261025T110455Z-2b96156ba364: diagnostic_png](</workspace/harness-conversation-runs/v05-newark-fixedtransport/.acycle/runs/20261025T110455Z-2b96156ba364/outputs/tuning.png>)
*中：年龄模型近线性；下：1575–1606 m 与 1910–1945 m 出现 ~8.5 cm/kyr 的短段（可能是多余极值）；trim 掉 72 行端点，无外推。*

时间域 MTM 与 EvoFFT（`20261025T110726Z-6e76718b431c`）：

![20261025T110726Z-6e76718b431c: spectrum_png](</workspace/harness-conversation-runs/v05-newark-fixedtransport/.acycle/runs/20261025T110726Z-6e76718b431c/outputs/spectrum.png>)
*417.4／393.6／405.1 kyr 居前三（功率 2.68／2.47／2.35），其后为 122.1、94.7、123.4、94.0 kyr。405 kyr 峰在很大程度上由调谐假设施加。*

![20261025T110726Z-6e76718b431c: evolution_png](</workspace/harness-conversation-runs/v05-newark-fixedtransport/.acycle/runs/20261025T110726Z-6e76718b431c/outputs/evolution.png>)
*2430 kyr 窗／405 kyr 步；低频 0.005–0.02 cyc/kyr 的能量在早期较强，405 kyr 附近为细窄弱带。*

谷分支对照（`20261025T111312Z-bc14efa3b318`）给出完全相同的周期组（417/394/405, 122/124/94 kyr），仅功率排序在小数位上互换——相位约定不改变时间域结论。

## 可靠性评估（核心）

**可以支持的**：(a) 深度序列中的 ~60 m 节律在整段剖面持续存在，且不受插值、重复值或零填充影响（本数据无需这些处理）；(b) 循环数 35 对峰/谷相位选择稳健；(c) 沉积速率沿剖面变化，而非恒定。

**不能支持的**：(a) 任何具体速率的统计显著性——COCO 全部 rate-global p≥0.95，eCOCO 最低仅触及 0.05 的可达下限，且 19 次模拟无法给出 p<0.05；(b) 九周期目标在 7 cm/kyr 处只有 6 个可分辨，短偏心率检验实际未被执行；(c) 405 kyr 时间域峰不是独立证据，它由控制点施加；(d) 调谐平均速率 14.1 cm/kyr 与 60 m÷405 kyr=14.8 cm/kyr 几乎相同，这来自假设本身，不构成验证。

**已知薄弱点**：原 `getpks` 无 prominence/最小间距判据，1575–1606 m 与 1910–1945 m 的短段提示可能存在多余极值；若某处漏计或错计一个周期，其下全部年龄将系统偏移 405 kyr。无正式年龄不确定度模型，未与独立 U–Pb 或磁性地层对比，也未建立该 2 km 剖面与已发表层位的逐行对应。

因此该结果应标为 **405 kyr 假设下的相对时间轴**：它提供了内部一致、可复算的深度—时间转换与时域诊断，但不是 Newark 的绝对年代学，也不是对 Olsen & Kent 原始标定的复现。

## 可下载产物

- 控制点／年龄模型：`20261025T110455Z-2b96156ba364/outputs/control_points.csv`、`age_model.csv`
- COCO 速率表：`20261025T105950Z-0531b1ec894c/outputs/coco.csv`、`null_max.csv`
- eCOCO 图与追踪速率：`20261025T110220Z-a5880602e02b/outputs/ecoco.csv`、`tracked_rate.csv`
- 各环节 `analysis.mat`、`provenance.json`、`.fig`／`.pdf` 均随运行保存

如需继续，建议二选一：把 COCO 模拟数提到 999 以上以获得可用的尾概率分辨率；或对 1575–1606 m 附近的极值做一次显式剔除的对照定年，检查循环数是否仍为 35。

# Sources and scientific scope

## Exact input and units

The bundled file is copied byte for byte from `data/Examples/Example-LateTriassicNewarkDepthRank.txt` in [Acycle commit dcba4279168745b563e0535b954297023dd62fc7](https://github.com/mingsongli/acycle/tree/dcba4279168745b563e0535b954297023dd62fc7). It has SHA-256 `1cd82c19c0de98a8c4d6f09d3af1fdb3ff2e07fe93c3ee241102dd75e4b65ac2` and 39,218 bytes. Its CR line endings are preserved. The existing MATLAB baseline reports 2,344 observations at 0–1999.60992 m and median spacing 0.85344 m.

The [original GUI callback](https://github.com/mingsongli/acycle/blob/dcba4279168745b563e0535b954297023dd62fc7/code/guicode/AC.m#L9097), `menu_example_Newark_Callback`, loads this exact filename and labels its axes `Depth (m)` and `Depth Rank`. Thus metres are sourced metadata, not guessed from the numbers. The [official Acycle v2.8 User's Guide](https://acycle.org/docs/Acycle_Users_Guide.pdf), printed p.38, identifies this exact file as the Newark Basin depth-rank example of Olsen and Kent (1996).

Olsen, P. E., and Kent, D. V. (1996). *Milankovitch climate forcing in the tropics of Pangaea during the Late Triassic*. Palaeogeography, Palaeoclimatology, Palaeoecology 122, 1–26. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-0182(95)00171-9).

We have not established the exact core/composite-section origin, orientation relative to absolute age, or a row-by-row mapping between this example and published age-control horizons. The filename alone does not supply those constraints. Cite Acycle and the original study when reusing the example. This package does not assign a new licence to the historical observations or redistribute the journal articles.

## External prior for the long cycle

Kent, D. V., and Olsen, P. E. (1999). *Astronomically tuned geomagnetic polarity timescale for the Late Triassic*. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 104(B6), 12831–12841. [DOI and publisher abstract](https://doi.org/10.1029/1999JB900076).

The abstract describes a roughly 5,000-m composite Newark section and states that its prominent 404-kyr eccentricity cycle has a mean thickness of about 60 m. This is the external basis for centring this demonstration's depth filter near 60 m. The 48–80 m nominal band is a declared teaching choice; it is not a confidence interval or a filter specification reproduced from that paper. The paper's long-cycle assignment is itself part of an astronomical calibration, not an independent determination that every 60-m feature in our example is orbital.

Kent, D. V., et al. (2018). *Empirical evidence for stability of the 405-kiloyear Jupiter–Venus eccentricity cycle over hundreds of millions of years*. PNAS 115(24), 6153–6158. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1800891115); [open full text](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6004457/).

Independent U–Pb zircon dates from the Chinle Formation, linked by magnetostratigraphy to the Newark–Hartford timescale, support the stability of the 405-kyr pacing back to at least about 215 Ma. This supports a regional astronomical hypothesis. It does not locate the supplied two-kilometre excerpt in absolute time or prove that an automatically selected filter extremum has the correct cycle number or phase. We use the modern nominal 405 kyr as an explicit assumption, rather than claiming to reproduce the 1999 paper's exact 404-kyr calibration.

<skill_content name="acycle-interpolation-pro">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-interpolation-pro
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Use `acycle_interpolate_pro` for a separately inspectable preprocessing run. Input is a numeric two-column coordinate/proxy file. Establish coordinate units and sample spacing first; interpolation does not create new independent observations or recover unresolved frequencies.

The MATLAB adapter extracts the numerical callback from Acycle `interpolationGUI.m`: `linear`, `nearest`, `next`, `previous`, `pchip`, `cubic`, `v5cubic`, `makima`, and `spline`. Choose a defensible method, normally linear for first exploration; use pchip when shape preservation is relevant. Explicit `dt` is in the coordinate unit. Omitted `dt` follows the original GUI median-spacing default.

`gap_policy=interpolate` is the GUI default. `gap_policy=zero` reproduces the GUI zero fill beyond `dt * gap_multiplier`, default multiplier 10; zero-filled gaps can produce spectral artifacts and are not observations. Inspect the gap report and figure. Do not silently zero-fill a hiatus. The `gui` endpoint policy preserves the original colon grid and its two-endpoint fallback when requested spacing exceeds the entire span; `strict_grid` rejects that fallback. Neither silently appends an off-grid final point.

Pass the saved `interpolated_csv` to subsequent MATLAB tools when regular sampling is wanted; keep the input receipt and preprocessing run ID. Do not reimplement interpolation or gap diagnosis in Python. Change a single option using `acycle_rerun`, preserving other settings. Report both requested and actual spacing and the resulting sample count.

Source/provenance: `docs/INTERPOLATION_TUNING_SOURCES.md` and `matlab/preparation_sources.json`. A passed bridge test establishes parity with the extracted original calculation, not validity of a particular geological interpolation choice.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-mini-robot">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-mini-robot
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Start from `acycle-intake`. Call `acycle_analyze` with `input_path`, optional `label`, and `parameters`. Baseline parameters are `detrend: lowess`, `span: 0.35`, `mtm_nw: 2`, and `evolution: true`; inspect the returned effective values for interpolation, frequency extent, smoothing and evolutionary window. These choices follow the pinned master workflow, not every historical Wiki setting.

MATLAB performs cleaning, interpolation, detrending, spectral calculation, evolutionary analysis and plotting. Prefer direct Acycle functions; GUI extractions require source attribution. Do not reproduce these numerical steps in Python. Store MATLAB-generated processed data, spectral tables and figures alongside the run response.

Inspect the original/processed series, trend, power spectrum, red-noise curves and evolutionary plot. Check coordinate units and confirm the frequency axis is reciprocal to those units. Flag broad trends, gaps, boundary effects, short windows and peaks close to Nyquist. Treat any listed strongest peaks as exploratory candidates, not automatic orbital identifications.

Use `acycle_get_run` to reopen saved results. If a computation fails, report its failed stage and dependency; never supply a Python substitute under the same run identity. Successful execution is distinct from direct-call parity and from scientific validation of an interpretation.

For follow-up requests use `acycle_rerun` with the selected baseline and only the requested parameter patch, or `acycle_sensitivity` for a one-parameter sweep. Preserve the baseline's method and data, retain the new parent link, and compare saved runs. Do not reconstruct the whole parameter set from memory or drop previously selected options.

Deliver the run ID, supported workflow executed, key artifacts, two or three observations, and limitations relevant to the user's question.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-coco">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-coco
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Use `acycle_coco` for a full-record or sliced COCO request and `acycle_ecoco` for evolutionary windows. These tools call the pinned Acycle v2 scientific cores; a paper using an earlier implementation is not automatically numerically equivalent. All calculations, Monte Carlo simulations and figures run in MATLAB. Python only sends parameters, preserves inputs and collects artifacts.

Require `depth_unit` and explicit `sedimentation_rate_min`, `sedimentation_rate_max`, `sedimentation_rate_step`, all rates in cm/kyr. State the geological basis for the range. Supply exactly one of `middle_age_ma` or `orbital_periods_kyr`; the former invokes Acycle's original age-dependent period calculation, the latter declares explicit periods in kyr. Do not invent the age to force a preferred optimum. Keep coordinate depth units, age in Ma, periods in kyr and rate in cm/kyr distinct.

This is a prerequisite, not optional reporting: when units, age/target or the basis of the rate range are missing, ask the user for them before any scientific tool call. Do not assume metres or an age, and do not start `acycle_analyze`/SWA as an unsolicited substitute for the requested rate plot. Import and structurally inspect the attachment first if useful. Read original CR/CRLF/LF files directly; line-ending conversion and shell `wc -l` are unnecessary. All numerical QA, including sample spacing and numerical ranges, must come from MATLAB results rather than Python/awk/shell calculations.

COCO `method: adaptive` maps to original adaptive9b and requires nine periods; `phase_averaged` maps to original adaptive and accepts 2–9 periods. eCOCO supports `adaptive`, `blocked` and `interleaved`, requires nine periods, and requires `window`/`step` in input depth units. Preserve unsupported/invalid-window information, and do not infer a continuous rate history across failed windows. The bridge uses complete windows without synthetic edge padding. Global nonlinear detrending is unavailable for blocked/interleaved modes because it would mix held-out information.

Inspect the current schema for optional detrending, `nfft`, `max_frequency`, `correlation`, `red_noise`, `nsim`, `seed`, and COCO-only `slices`. Record effective parameters. Default 199 simulations and local smoke settings such as 19 simulations are not interchangeable with a publication's Monte Carlo design. Choose simulation count from the required tail resolution and computational budget, not from the desired significance. A fixed seed makes runs reproducible; it does not remove Monte Carlo uncertainty.

Read original output labels and method notes to distinguish correlation, pointwise p-values, search/global statistics, target support and any held-out criterion. Never relabel a pointwise result as control over all rates, windows and parameter choices. The largest correlation need not be the most defensible chronology. Compare with independent age constraints and report alternative optima.

For conversational changes use `acycle_rerun` with the saved `run_id` and only the requested `parameter_patch`; use `acycle_sensitivity` for a one-parameter sweep. This preserves COCO versus eCOCO, the method, target, seed and input unless explicitly changed. Do not send these adjustments to `acycle_analyze`. Compare grid ranges, spacing, targets, detrending, windows, red-noise choices and Monte Carlo count. Preserve a declared baseline before exploratory steering. For paper tasks, obtain the full distribution's `benchmarks/` source records or the repository at https://github.com/JFjifang/Acycle_Harness/tree/main/benchmarks; verify the exact interval, columns and hashes. Report separately the original-function parity, authentic-data workflow, matched published quantitative criterion, and remaining differences.

A backend failure is reported with its saved run ID and diagnostics. Do not repair authentication with `gh auth`, silently retry, change backends or replace the calculation in Python. Preserve the failed evidence and wait for the user to resolve the execution environment or request another attempt.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-astronomical-tuning">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-astronomical-tuning
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Use `acycle_tune` on a saved MATLAB `filtered_csv` (coordinate, filtered signal, optional envelope) or a two-column bandpassed curve. Read the filter run and inspect its plotted curve first. Establish the depth unit, filtering band, target full-cycle period in kyr, selected extrema, and age convention. Do not invent an absolute age anchor from a spectral peak.

Require explicit `period_kyr`, `anchor_age_kyr`, `anchor_phase` (`peak` or `trough`), `extrema` (`peaks`, `troughs`, or `both`), and `depth_unit`. The original Acycle `getpks` identifies extrema without an invented Python peak detector. Same-phase controls advance a full period; alternating peaks and troughs advance half periods. The first selected anchor-phase extremum receives the anchor age, so a preceding opposite-phase control can have a negative relative time. Flat/ambiguous extrema and failure to alternate require inspection, not silent point removal. These automatically proposed controls are a hypothesis and need geological review.

Default `endpoint_policy=trim` keeps the control-point-covered interval. `linear_extrapolate` explicitly extends endpoint slopes and must be disclosed. `error` rejects uncovered samples. Examine `control_points_csv`, `age_model_csv`, the three-panel diagnostic, sedimentation-rate behavior and discarded endpoints. All numerical conversion and plots are MATLAB, using original `depthtotime`.

For the time-domain diagnostic call `acycle_analyze` with the ORIGINAL proxy input and `tuning_run_id` pointing to the completed tuning run. This applies its saved MATLAB age model and covered coordinate range, with artifact hash verification. Do not diagnose only `tuned_csv` and use its imposed period as proof. Specify output `coordinate_unit=kyr`, a justified time sampling interval, and time-domain evolutionary windows. Interpolation spacing is not independent temporal resolution.

Present the selected band, period, phase, relative/absolute anchor and boundary policy alongside the result. Orbital agreement caused by tuning is conditional; independent ages, untuned bands, alternate controls and sensitivity checks are needed for a stronger chronology claim. Rerunning tuning creates a new model; rerun the original proxy with that new `tuning_run_id` to update the time diagnostic.

Source/provenance: `docs/INTERPOLATION_TUNING_SOURCES.md` and `matlab/preparation_sources.json`. Do not conflate this extrema-based bridge with the entire interactive Acycle astronomical tuning GUI or a validated automatic age model.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-spectral-interpretation">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-spectral-interpretation
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Read the saved MATLAB result using `acycle_get_run`. Check detrending, interpolation interval, time-bandwidth product, spectral smoothing, spectral resolution and coordinate units before interpreting peaks. Use `acycle_analyze` for a changed parameter set, preserving `parent_run_id` and assigning a new label.

Confidence curves are pointwise relative to their stated background model. Searching many frequencies, windows or parameter settings increases false-positive opportunities. Neither a threshold crossing nor a filtered oscillation alone demonstrates astronomical forcing. Explicitly distinguish observation, hypothesis and independent corroboration.

For a user-selected band, pass `filter_band: [low, high]` in reciprocal coordinate units and a supported `filter_method` (`gaussian` or `taner_hilbert`). Validate that the requested range lies within available frequencies. MATLAB must compute filtering, Hilbert envelopes and figures. Record the chosen band before comparing its output with orbital periods; do not select and confirm a band on the same evidence without acknowledging selection.

Compare peaks and evolutionary persistence across reasonable detrending or sampling settings with `acycle_sensitivity` and `acycle_compare`. Run the official red-noise control when validating a workflow. Explain that random noise can still exhibit pointwise exceedances; the negative control is not required to have zero peaks.

If the requested significance test is unavailable, state that limitation. A new method may be added as a clearly labeled extension, preferably MATLAB, with the model and assumptions retained. Do not rename an approximation as Acycle's original test.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-sensitivity-steering">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-sensitivity-steering
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Open the relevant baseline with `acycle_get_run`. Resolve phrases such as "the previous figure" or "the original result" from the actual conversation and saved run IDs; do not assume that the latest created run is always the requested baseline. Translate only the user's requested changes into parameters. For one or several changes use `acycle_rerun` with `run_id`, `parameter_patch`, and an explanatory `label`. For a one-parameter sweep use `acycle_sensitivity` with `run_id`, `parameter`, and `values`.

`acycle_rerun` preserves the frozen input, original operation (`analyze`, `swa`, `coco`, or `ecoco`), effective defaults and other settings. Omitted parameters stay fixed. Never route a COCO/eCOCO/SWA adjustment through `acycle_analyze`. The core rejects a direct call whose `parent_run_id` belongs to another operation, and rejects omitted settings that would reset the parent's method. A user-requested change to a different operation starts a new independent analysis with its matching tool; compare its run ID with the original instead of assigning a false same-method parent.

Keep `method`, target definition, seed, correlation and units unless the user explicitly changes them. `parameter_patch` may use null to remove an optional field or restore a MATLAB default, but `method` and `detrend` require an explicit valid choice and cannot be reset with null. Switching an astronomical target between age and periods replaces the other target; switching `span` and `detrend_window` replaces the other window definition. Switching to linear COCO/eCOCO detrending removes an inapplicable span/window. Read the returned `steering.removed_or_reset_parameters` and explain those consequences. An incompatible change must be resolved explicitly, not replaced with another method to obtain a successful run.

A typical detrending check is `parameter: span`, `values: [0.25, 0.35, 0.45]`. These are experiments, not an optimization objective for maximizing significance. Changes to sample spacing, filtering bands, evolutionary windows and age assumptions need a scientific reason and correct units.

Run every scientific branch in MATLAB. Keep the baseline's input, parameters and outputs immutable. Check matching input hashes, the preserved operation, and the child's `parent_run_id`. Retrieve the new run IDs and use `acycle_compare` with `run_ids`. Compare coordinate domains and units before comparing peaks. Python may assemble saved summaries; any newly computed scientific diagnostic or comparison figure belongs in MATLAB. Present the returned MATLAB figures and saved-file attachments when the client exposes them; a file path alone is not evidence that the chat UI displayed a figure.

Explain what changed, what remained stable and what depends on the chosen settings. Do not present the most favorable branch alone or hide failed branches. Keep selected and rejected alternatives in the run record so a later user can retrace the decision.

For requests beyond Acycle, prefer extending its MATLAB interface. Python can handle genuinely missing capabilities or temporary user-specific extensions, but label their provenance and return their numeric output to MATLAB for subsequent Acycle analysis and plotting.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

## 四个主要观察

**1. 深度中存在持续的 ~60 m 节律。** MTM 前三峰 57.16 m、61.36 m、53.78 m（稳健 AR(1) ρ=0.43，点态均超 95%），另有 270/238 m 的低频能量。谱峰落在预先声明的 48–80 m 带内而**不在其中心**，说明它并非纯粹由选带造成；但选带来自 Kent & Olsen (1999) 的区域先验，仍属探索性候选。

**2. 速率搜索没有得到统计支持。** COCO 最佳 7 cm/kyr（Spearman ρ=0.378），但 **21 个速率的 rate-global p 全部 ≥0.95**；19 个 AR(1) 替代序列的最大相关为 0.369–0.450，观测值正落在其中间。7 cm/kyr 处仅 **6/9** 个目标周期可分辨（全九周期解需 ≥9.66 cm/kyr）。eCOCO 逐窗 global p 最低 0.05（仅 600–900 m），1200–1500 m 全部为 1，且不跨窗校正。**因此短偏心率检验未获证实**；19 次模拟本身也不可能达到 p<0.05。

**3. 沿剖面速率并非常数。** eCOCO 追踪速率自 300 m 的 6 cm/kyr 单调升至 1600 m 的 13 cm/kyr（294 个有限格点，0 个未解点）；定年隐含的 35 段速率为 7.6–17.1 cm/kyr。两条独立途径在"变速率"上一致，但绝对值系统性偏差约一倍。

**4. 循环计数对相位选择稳健。** 峰分支与谷分支各自独立选出 **35 个极值**，均覆盖 0–13 770 kyr。这是本方案中最实质的可靠性证据——计数不依赖"峰或谷"约定。

</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Use this skill only when the user explicitly chooses the Newark demonstration and supplies the corresponding official example file. This is a workflow-guided demonstration, not unrestricted blind method selection. Locate and read the adjacent demo package's `manifest.json` and `SOURCES.md`; the manifest is two directories above this skill directory. Verify that the imported/workspace input hash matches the manifest. If another file is supplied, establish its scientific context rather than applying Newark parameters.

Tell the user briefly that you are using the public demonstration assumptions: a 405-kyr relative chronology, 210 Ma only for approximate orbital target periods, and 19 simulations for quick exploration. Loading this named demonstration constitutes permission to use its declared priors; no repeated confirmation is needed. If the user changes the study assumptions, preserve the earlier version and make the change explicit.

Use the installed Acycle intake, mini-robot, COCO, age-model and sensitivity skills together with the current tool schemas. Inspect supported capabilities. Import the current authorized attachment using the host bridge, or use its exact workspace path. Preserve raw bytes and source attribution. Every numerical operation, extrema selection, interpolation, tuning and figure must execute in MATLAB using Acycle sources. Python may transport files, coordinate requests and present artifacts. Do not use Python/NumPy to derive numeric QA, spectral results, control points or charts.

Follow the public research sequence, retaining the manifest settings unless the user requests a change:

1. Establish input units and numerical quality in MATLAB through original Acycle Interpolation Pro, using the manifest's interpolation preset. Retain the original input and the actual `interpolated_csv` output, grid/gap diagnostic and source linkage. Do not replace the 0.85344-m example grid with the differently sourced 0.85-m grid.
2. Run original Acycle preprocessing, depth-domain MTM and EvoFFT on that Interpolation Pro artifact with the manifest's depth preset. The depth analysis may also generate the declared Gaussian filtered artifact in the same MATLAB pass; reuse that actual output to avoid redundant computation.
3. Run full-record COCO and complete-window eCOCO on the same Interpolation Pro artifact with the manifest presets. Keep the 5–25 cm/kyr grid, resolved-period counts, NaN cells and original Monte Carlo outputs. The period/age prior is supplied context, never a number inferred from the strongest observed peak.
4. Use the actual MATLAB filtered file as input to the supported tuning operation. Extract maxima in MATLAB; assign the first selected maximum relative time zero and consecutive maxima 405-kyr spacing. Keep the manifest's trim policy. Use Acycle tuning/interpolation and retain the controls, selected extrema, full provenance and age-depth figure. If extrema are insufficient or controls are invalid, report that stage instead of inventing a usable chronology.
5. Analyse the original raw proxy in relative time through the completed tuning run's controls, using the supported `tuning_run_id` linkage and manifest time-diagnostic preset. Do not feed the narrow-band filtered output to this diagnostic. Respect the trimmed control range and report the actual regridding used. The raw source hash differs from the formatted Interpolation Pro output hash; preserve both and their lineage.
6. Return key original MATLAB images, downloadable source artifacts and a short interpretation. Mark the chronology “405 kyr假设下的相对时间轴”. Include no more than a few main observations in the conversation; preserve tables and technical provenance in artifacts.

Use live, newly completed outputs. Reopening a saved run is allowed when explicitly presenting that saved result; label its origin. Never replace a failed live calculation with a successful rehearsal result, hide a parameter search, silently substitute another method, or convert this scenario's deliverable list into a claim that all stages passed.

Interpretation requirements:

- A depth spectrum peak is an exploratory candidate. Do not assign astronomical names by appearance alone.
- The 60-m centre is a sourced regional prior; the 48–80 m nominal bandwidth is an explicit demo choice. It was not chosen by matching this run's strongest peak.
- Use rate-global COCO Monte Carlo results. eCOCO's global correction applies within each window, not across the full map. With 19 simulations, do not claim p < 0.05.
- Inspect target resolution at candidate rates; retain unresolved cells and multiple candidate ridges. An all-NaN map is an unresolved stage, not evidence of no orbital forcing and not permission to search silently for a pleasing map.
- A 405-kyr time-spectrum peak is partly imposed by the tuning hypothesis. Other time-domain peaks also depend on this model; neither supplies independent absolute dating.
- Peak/trough selection is a phase convention. The first control's relative zero is not an absolute age. No formal age uncertainty model is provided.
- EvoFFT's zero-padded edges and eCOCO's unpadded complete windows have different support. Do not interpret map edges as equally constrained.

For a follow-up, use saved-run steering where supported and change only requested parameters. In particular, an eCOCO window/step change remains the original eCOCO method. A tuning-phase change starts from the same filtered file, retains period and endpoint policy, creates new controls and then reapplies them to the original proxy. A depth-only detrending request does not authorize quietly rebuilding all derived chronologies. Keep parent links, input hashes and actual effective parameters. Compare before and after using saved MATLAB results.

Do not promise a 3–5-minute live completion time. That interval is a possible speaking plan; execution time depends on the actual backend and client. Numerical completion, artifact delivery and pixels rendered in the user's client are separate observations.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_resources>

</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Use `acycle_capabilities` to check the configured backend. When the user supplies a Harness file attachment and the tool list exposes `acycle_import_attachment`, call it to obtain the workspace `input_path`. A single file in the latest attached user message can be imported without arguments; with multiple files, select an `attachment_id` from the returned candidates according to the user's request. Do not search another session's attachments or guess a storage path. When that Harness-only tool is unavailable (for example through MCP), use a file already in the current workspace. Run `acycle_inspect` on the resolved path. Distinguish a depth series from an age series, identify the proxy and units, and preserve the original file. Establish whether the user wants exploratory periodicity, a specified hypothesis, or a chronology. Infer metadata from an accompanying paper or table before asking for missing information.

Numerical processing and plots must run in MATLAB. Python is for Harness integration, transport and metadata; never silently switch to a Python analytical fallback when MATLAB is missing. Report an unavailable backend precisely and keep the request ready to rerun.

The inspect result is structural: `logical_line_count` counts CR, CRLF and LF consistently, and is not a validated sample count. Original Acycle/MATLAB reads all three newline formats. A CR-only file is not a one-row dataset; do not reinterpret it with `wc -l` or normalize it into an unnecessary LF copy. Keep the imported exact bytes and hash. Use the preview for column meaning only. Do not calculate spacing, min/max, means, trends, spectrum statistics, missing-value counts or other routine numerical QA with Python, awk or shell arithmetic; normal Acycle scientific checks belong in MATLAB and appear in the completed result. User-authorized extensions for features genuinely absent from Acycle remain allowed, with their provenance stated and a MATLAB bridge preferred.

For a sedimentation-rate plot, rate history, age model or chronology request, first establish coordinate units and the appropriate supplied chronological basis. COCO/eCOCO inference requires an explicit age/astronomical target and the scientific basis of its rate-search range; conversion using a user-provided rate or age-depth controls instead uses those supplied constraints. If a required assumption is absent from supplied metadata, ask a concise question before launching any scientific analysis. Do not label metres as "assumed", infer an age from a filename, or run mini-robot/SWA as a substitute while those requirements are missing. Attachment import and structural inspection may proceed; an unrequested preliminary spectrum does not resolve missing geological constraints.

Use the first two numeric columns only when their meaning is clear. Check duplicate coordinates, missing observations, sorting, irregular sampling and large gaps in the MATLAB result. Duplicate handling and interpolation change the effective dataset and must be visible in the report. Do not turn depth wavelengths into kyr without a stated rate or age-depth model.

Choose the operation from the scientific question and sampling, without making the user supply tool names or JSON. `acycle_analyze` provides a first exploratory mini-robot spectrum/evolution workflow. For a request about false discoveries across a spectrum, consider the SWA skill and its sampling constraints. For explicitly constrained sedimentation-rate or evolutionary-rate testing, use the COCO/eCOCO skill; geological age/targets and a justified rate range cannot be invented from the proxy alone. Use a descriptive label and record the returned run ID, effective parameters, MATLAB/Acycle provenance and artifacts. If the requested feature is outside the bridged subset, say so and prefer a small MATLAB adapter to the installed Acycle routines.

In follow-up conversation, use `acycle_rerun` or `acycle_sensitivity` on the selected saved run. Preserve its analysis operation and untouched parameters; a request to change plot range, span, window or simulation count does not itself request a different method. Use the steering skill for branching and comparison.

Return a concise dataset summary, important assumptions, available analysis path, and the next scientific decision. Do not imply that basic file inspection constitutes numerical quality control or that a successful API call means an analysis succeeded.

If the configured MATLAB/GitHub backend fails, retain and report the failed run ID, saved diagnostics and precise failure. Do not invoke `gh auth`, replace credentials, change the backend, retry the computation, or recreate it with Python on your own. The user can decide when the environment is ready for another attempt; a backend error is not a request to alter scientific data or methods.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

# Sources and scientific scope

## Exact input and units

The bundled file is copied byte for byte from `data/Examples/Example-LateTriassicNewarkDepthRank.txt` in [Acycle commit dcba4279168745b563e0535b954297023dd62fc7](https://github.com/mingsongli/acycle/tree/dcba4279168745b563e0535b954297023dd62fc7). It has SHA-256 `1cd82c19c0de98a8c4d6f09d3af1fdb3ff2e07fe93c3ee241102dd75e4b65ac2` and 39,218 bytes. Its CR line endings are preserved. The existing MATLAB baseline reports 2,344 observations at 0–1999.60992 m and median spacing 0.85344 m.

The [original GUI callback](https://github.com/mingsongli/acycle/blob/dcba4279168745b563e0535b954297023dd62fc7/code/guicode/AC.m#L9097), `menu_example_Newark_Callback`, loads this exact filename and labels its axes `Depth (m)` and `Depth Rank`. Thus metres are sourced metadata, not guessed from the numbers. The [official Acycle v2.8 User's Guide](https://acycle.org/docs/Acycle_Users_Guide.pdf), printed p.38, identifies this exact file as the Newark Basin depth-rank example of Olsen and Kent (1996).

Olsen, P. E., and Kent, D. V. (1996). *Milankovitch climate forcing in the tropics of Pangaea during the Late Triassic*. Palaeogeography, Palaeoclimatology, Palaeoecology 122, 1–26. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-0182(95)00171-9).

We have not established the exact core/composite-section origin, orientation relative to absolute age, or a row-by-row mapping between this example and published age-control horizons. The filename alone does not supply those constraints. Cite Acycle and the original study when reusing the example. This package does not assign a new licence to the historical observations or redistribute the journal articles.

## External prior for the long cycle

Kent, D. V., and Olsen, P. E. (1999). *Astronomically tuned geomagnetic polarity timescale for the Late Triassic*. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 104(B6), 12831–12841. [DOI and publisher abstract](https://doi.org/10.1029/1999JB900076).

The abstract describes a roughly 5,000-m composite Newark section and states that its prominent 404-kyr eccentricity cycle has a mean thickness of about 60 m. This is the external basis for centring this demonstration's depth filter near 60 m. The 48–80 m nominal band is a declared teaching choice; it is not a confidence interval or a filter specification reproduced from that paper. The paper's long-cycle assignment is itself part of an astronomical calibration, not an independent determination that every 60-m feature in our example is orbital.

Kent, D. V., et al. (2018). *Empirical evidence for stability of the 405-kiloyear Jupiter–Venus eccentricity cycle over hundreds of millions of years*. PNAS 115(24), 6153–6158. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1800891115); [open full text](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6004457/).

Independent U–Pb zircon dates from the Chinle Formation, linked by magnetostratigraphy to the Newark–Hartford timescale, support the stability of the 405-kyr pacing back to at least about 215 Ma. This supports a regional astronomical hypothesis. It does not locate the supplied two-kilometre excerpt in absolute time or prove that an automatically selected filter extremum has the correct cycle number or phase. We use the modern nominal 405 kyr as an explicit assumption, rather than claiming to reproduce the 1999 paper's exact 404-kyr calibration.

<skill_content name="acycle-interpolation-pro">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-interpolation-pro
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Use `acycle_interpolate_pro` for a separately inspectable preprocessing run. Input is a numeric two-column coordinate/proxy file. Establish coordinate units and sample spacing first; interpolation does not create new independent observations or recover unresolved frequencies.

The MATLAB adapter extracts the numerical callback from Acycle `interpolationGUI.m`: `linear`, `nearest`, `next`, `previous`, `pchip`, `cubic`, `v5cubic`, `makima`, and `spline`. Choose a defensible method, normally linear for first exploration; use pchip when shape preservation is relevant. Explicit `dt` is in the coordinate unit. Omitted `dt` follows the original GUI median-spacing default.

`gap_policy=interpolate` is the GUI default. `gap_policy=zero` reproduces the GUI zero fill beyond `dt * gap_multiplier`, default multiplier 10; zero-filled gaps can produce spectral artifacts and are not observations. Inspect the gap report and figure. Do not silently zero-fill a hiatus. The `gui` endpoint policy preserves the original colon grid and its two-endpoint fallback when requested spacing exceeds the entire span; `strict_grid` rejects that fallback. Neither silently appends an off-grid final point.

Pass the saved `interpolated_csv` to subsequent MATLAB tools when regular sampling is wanted; keep the input receipt and preprocessing run ID. Do not reimplement interpolation or gap diagnosis in Python. Change a single option using `acycle_rerun`, preserving other settings. Report both requested and actual spacing and the resulting sample count.

Source/provenance: `docs/INTERPOLATION_TUNING_SOURCES.md` and `matlab/preparation_sources.json`. A passed bridge test establishes parity with the extracted original calculation, not validity of a particular geological interpolation choice.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-mini-robot">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-mini-robot
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Start from `acycle-intake`. Call `acycle_analyze` with `input_path`, optional `label`, and `parameters`. Baseline parameters are `detrend: lowess`, `span: 0.35`, `mtm_nw: 2`, and `evolution: true`; inspect the returned effective values for interpolation, frequency extent, smoothing and evolutionary window. These choices follow the pinned master workflow, not every historical Wiki setting.

MATLAB performs cleaning, interpolation, detrending, spectral calculation, evolutionary analysis and plotting. Prefer direct Acycle functions; GUI extractions require source attribution. Do not reproduce these numerical steps in Python. Store MATLAB-generated processed data, spectral tables and figures alongside the run response.

Inspect the original/processed series, trend, power spectrum, red-noise curves and evolutionary plot. Check coordinate units and confirm the frequency axis is reciprocal to those units. Flag broad trends, gaps, boundary effects, short windows and peaks close to Nyquist. Treat any listed strongest peaks as exploratory candidates, not automatic orbital identifications.

Use `acycle_get_run` to reopen saved results. If a computation fails, report its failed stage and dependency; never supply a Python substitute under the same run identity. Successful execution is distinct from direct-call parity and from scientific validation of an interpretation.

For follow-up requests use `acycle_rerun` with the selected baseline and only the requested parameter patch, or `acycle_sensitivity` for a one-parameter sweep. Preserve the baseline's method and data, retain the new parent link, and compare saved runs. Do not reconstruct the whole parameter set from memory or drop previously selected options.

Deliver the run ID, supported workflow executed, key artifacts, two or three observations, and limitations relevant to the user's question.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-coco">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-coco
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Use `acycle_coco` for a full-record or sliced COCO request and `acycle_ecoco` for evolutionary windows. These tools call the pinned Acycle v2 scientific cores; a paper using an earlier implementation is not automatically numerically equivalent. All calculations, Monte Carlo simulations and figures run in MATLAB. Python only sends parameters, preserves inputs and collects artifacts.

Require `depth_unit` and explicit `sedimentation_rate_min`, `sedimentation_rate_max`, `sedimentation_rate_step`, all rates in cm/kyr. State the geological basis for the range. Supply exactly one of `middle_age_ma` or `orbital_periods_kyr`; the former invokes Acycle's original age-dependent period calculation, the latter declares explicit periods in kyr. Do not invent the age to force a preferred optimum. Keep coordinate depth units, age in Ma, periods in kyr and rate in cm/kyr distinct.

This is a prerequisite, not optional reporting: when units, age/target or the basis of the rate range are missing, ask the user for them before any scientific tool call. Do not assume metres or an age, and do not start `acycle_analyze`/SWA as an unsolicited substitute for the requested rate plot. Import and structurally inspect the attachment first if useful. Read original CR/CRLF/LF files directly; line-ending conversion and shell `wc -l` are unnecessary. All numerical QA, including sample spacing and numerical ranges, must come from MATLAB results rather than Python/awk/shell calculations.

COCO `method: adaptive` maps to original adaptive9b and requires nine periods; `phase_averaged` maps to original adaptive and accepts 2–9 periods. eCOCO supports `adaptive`, `blocked` and `interleaved`, requires nine periods, and requires `window`/`step` in input depth units. Preserve unsupported/invalid-window information, and do not infer a continuous rate history across failed windows. The bridge uses complete windows without synthetic edge padding. Global nonlinear detrending is unavailable for blocked/interleaved modes because it would mix held-out information.

Inspect the current schema for optional detrending, `nfft`, `max_frequency`, `correlation`, `red_noise`, `nsim`, `seed`, and COCO-only `slices`. Record effective parameters. Default 199 simulations and local smoke settings such as 19 simulations are not interchangeable with a publication's Monte Carlo design. Choose simulation count from the required tail resolution and computational budget, not from the desired significance. A fixed seed makes runs reproducible; it does not remove Monte Carlo uncertainty.

Read original output labels and method notes to distinguish correlation, pointwise p-values, search/global statistics, target support and any held-out criterion. Never relabel a pointwise result as control over all rates, windows and parameter choices. The largest correlation need not be the most defensible chronology. Compare with independent age constraints and report alternative optima.

For conversational changes use `acycle_rerun` with the saved `run_id` and only the requested `parameter_patch`; use `acycle_sensitivity` for a one-parameter sweep. This preserves COCO versus eCOCO, the method, target, seed and input unless explicitly changed. Do not send these adjustments to `acycle_analyze`. Compare grid ranges, spacing, targets, detrending, windows, red-noise choices and Monte Carlo count. Preserve a declared baseline before exploratory steering. For paper tasks, obtain the full distribution's `benchmarks/` source records or the repository at https://github.com/JFjifang/Acycle_Harness/tree/main/benchmarks; verify the exact interval, columns and hashes. Report separately the original-function parity, authentic-data workflow, matched published quantitative criterion, and remaining differences.

A backend failure is reported with its saved run ID and diagnostics. Do not repair authentication with `gh auth`, silently retry, change backends or replace the calculation in Python. Preserve the failed evidence and wait for the user to resolve the execution environment or request another attempt.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-astronomical-tuning">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-astronomical-tuning
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Use `acycle_tune` on a saved MATLAB `filtered_csv` (coordinate, filtered signal, optional envelope) or a two-column bandpassed curve. Read the filter run and inspect its plotted curve first. Establish the depth unit, filtering band, target full-cycle period in kyr, selected extrema, and age convention. Do not invent an absolute age anchor from a spectral peak.

Require explicit `period_kyr`, `anchor_age_kyr`, `anchor_phase` (`peak` or `trough`), `extrema` (`peaks`, `troughs`, or `both`), and `depth_unit`. The original Acycle `getpks` identifies extrema without an invented Python peak detector. Same-phase controls advance a full period; alternating peaks and troughs advance half periods. The first selected anchor-phase extremum receives the anchor age, so a preceding opposite-phase control can have a negative relative time. Flat/ambiguous extrema and failure to alternate require inspection, not silent point removal. These automatically proposed controls are a hypothesis and need geological review.

Default `endpoint_policy=trim` keeps the control-point-covered interval. `linear_extrapolate` explicitly extends endpoint slopes and must be disclosed. `error` rejects uncovered samples. Examine `control_points_csv`, `age_model_csv`, the three-panel diagnostic, sedimentation-rate behavior and discarded endpoints. All numerical conversion and plots are MATLAB, using original `depthtotime`.

For the time-domain diagnostic call `acycle_analyze` with the ORIGINAL proxy input and `tuning_run_id` pointing to the completed tuning run. This applies its saved MATLAB age model and covered coordinate range, with artifact hash verification. Do not diagnose only `tuned_csv` and use its imposed period as proof. Specify output `coordinate_unit=kyr`, a justified time sampling interval, and time-domain evolutionary windows. Interpolation spacing is not independent temporal resolution.

Present the selected band, period, phase, relative/absolute anchor and boundary policy alongside the result. Orbital agreement caused by tuning is conditional; independent ages, untuned bands, alternate controls and sensitivity checks are needed for a stronger chronology claim. Rerunning tuning creates a new model; rerun the original proxy with that new `tuning_run_id` to update the time diagnostic.

Source/provenance: `docs/INTERPOLATION_TUNING_SOURCES.md` and `matlab/preparation_sources.json`. Do not conflate this extrema-based bridge with the entire interactive Acycle astronomical tuning GUI or a validated automatic age model.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-spectral-interpretation">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-spectral-interpretation
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Read the saved MATLAB result using `acycle_get_run`. Check detrending, interpolation interval, time-bandwidth product, spectral smoothing, spectral resolution and coordinate units before interpreting peaks. Use `acycle_analyze` for a changed parameter set, preserving `parent_run_id` and assigning a new label.

Confidence curves are pointwise relative to their stated background model. Searching many frequencies, windows or parameter settings increases false-positive opportunities. Neither a threshold crossing nor a filtered oscillation alone demonstrates astronomical forcing. Explicitly distinguish observation, hypothesis and independent corroboration.

For a user-selected band, pass `filter_band: [low, high]` in reciprocal coordinate units and a supported `filter_method` (`gaussian` or `taner_hilbert`). Validate that the requested range lies within available frequencies. MATLAB must compute filtering, Hilbert envelopes and figures. Record the chosen band before comparing its output with orbital periods; do not select and confirm a band on the same evidence without acknowledging selection.

Compare peaks and evolutionary persistence across reasonable detrending or sampling settings with `acycle_sensitivity` and `acycle_compare`. Run the official red-noise control when validating a workflow. Explain that random noise can still exhibit pointwise exceedances; the negative control is not required to have zero peaks.

If the requested significance test is unavailable, state that limitation. A new method may be added as a clearly labeled extension, preferably MATLAB, with the model and assumptions retained. Do not rename an approximation as Acycle's original test.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_content name="acycle-sensitivity-steering">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /workspace/Acycle_Harness/plugin/skills/acycle-sensitivity-steering
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>

Open the relevant baseline with `acycle_get_run`. Resolve phrases such as "the previous figure" or "the original result" from the actual conversation and saved run IDs; do not assume that the latest created run is always the requested baseline. Translate only the user's requested changes into parameters. For one or several changes use `acycle_rerun` with `run_id`, `parameter_patch`, and an explanatory `label`. For a one-parameter sweep use `acycle_sensitivity` with `run_id`, `parameter`, and `values`.

`acycle_rerun` preserves the frozen input, original operation (`analyze`, `swa`, `coco`, or `ecoco`), effective defaults and other settings. Omitted parameters stay fixed. Never route a COCO/eCOCO/SWA adjustment through `acycle_analyze`. The core rejects a direct call whose `parent_run_id` belongs to another operation, and rejects omitted settings that would reset the parent's method. A user-requested change to a different operation starts a new independent analysis with its matching tool; compare its run ID with the original instead of assigning a false same-method parent.

Keep `method`, target definition, seed, correlation and units unless the user explicitly changes them. `parameter_patch` may use null to remove an optional field or restore a MATLAB default, but `method` and `detrend` require an explicit valid choice and cannot be reset with null. Switching an astronomical target between age and periods replaces the other target; switching `span` and `detrend_window` replaces the other window definition. Switching to linear COCO/eCOCO detrending removes an inapplicable span/window. Read the returned `steering.removed_or_reset_parameters` and explain those consequences. An incompatible change must be resolved explicitly, not replaced with another method to obtain a successful run.

A typical detrending check is `parameter: span`, `values: [0.25, 0.35, 0.45]`. These are experiments, not an optimization objective for maximizing significance. Changes to sample spacing, filtering bands, evolutionary windows and age assumptions need a scientific reason and correct units.

Run every scientific branch in MATLAB. Keep the baseline's input, parameters and outputs immutable. Check matching input hashes, the preserved operation, and the child's `parent_run_id`. Retrieve the new run IDs and use `acycle_compare` with `run_ids`. Compare coordinate domains and units before comparing peaks. Python may assemble saved summaries; any newly computed scientific diagnostic or comparison figure belongs in MATLAB. Present the returned MATLAB figures and saved-file attachments when the client exposes them; a file path alone is not evidence that the chat UI displayed a figure.

Explain what changed, what remained stable and what depends on the chosen settings. Do not present the most favorable branch alone or hide failed branches. Keep selected and rejected alternatives in the run record so a later user can retrace the decision.

For requests beyond Acycle, prefer extending its MATLAB interface. Python can handle genuinely missing capabilities or temporary user-specific extensions, but label their provenance and return their numeric output to MATLAB for subsequent Acycle analysis and plotting.

</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

## 四个主要观察

**1. 深度中存在持续的 ~60 m 节律。** MTM 前三峰 57.16 m、61.36 m、53.78 m（稳健 AR(1) ρ=0.43，点态均超 95%），另有 270/238 m 的低频能量。谱峰落在预先声明的 48–80 m 带内而**不在其中心**，说明它并非纯粹由选带造成；但选带来自 Kent & Olsen (1999) 的区域先验，仍属探索性候选。

**2. 速率搜索没有得到统计支持。** COCO 最佳 7 cm/kyr（Spearman ρ=0.378），但 **21 个速率的 rate-global p 全部 ≥0.95**；19 个 AR(1) 替代序列的最大相关为 0.369–0.450，观测值正落在其中间。7 cm/kyr 处仅 **6/9** 个目标周期可分辨（全九周期解需 ≥9.66 cm/kyr）。eCOCO 逐窗 global p 最低 0.05（仅 600–900 m），1200–1500 m 全部为 1，且不跨窗校正。**因此短偏心率检验未获证实**；19 次模拟本身也不可能达到 p<0.05。

**3. 沿剖面速率并非常数。** eCOCO 追踪速率自 300 m 的 6 cm/kyr 单调升至 1600 m 的 13 cm/kyr（294 个有限格点，0 个未解点）；定年隐含的 35 段速率为 7.6–17.1 cm/kyr。两条独立途径在"变速率"上一致，但绝对值系统性偏差约一倍。

**4. 循环计数对相位选择稳健。** 峰分支与谷分支各自独立选出 **35 个极值**，均覆盖 0–13 770 kyr。这是本方案中最实质的可靠性证据——计数不依赖"峰或谷"约定。

## 可靠性评估（核心）

**可以支持的**：(a) 深度序列中的 ~60 m 节律在整段剖面持续存在，且不受插值、重复值或零填充影响（本数据无需这些处理）；(b) 循环数 35 对峰/谷相位选择稳健；(c) 沉积速率沿剖面变化，而非恒定。

**已知薄弱点**：原 `getpks` 无 prominence/最小间距判据，1575–1606 m 与 1910–1945 m 的短段提示可能存在多余极值；若某处漏计或错计一个周期，其下全部年龄将系统偏移 405 kyr。无正式年龄不确定度模型，未与独立 U–Pb 或磁性地层对比，也未建立该 2 km 剖面与已发表层位的逐行对应。

因此该结果应标为 **405 kyr 假设下的相对时间轴**：它提供了内部一致、可复算的深度—时间转换与时域诊断，但不是 Newark 的绝对年代学，也不是对 Olsen & Kent 原始标定的复现。

## 四个主要观察

**1. 深度中存在持续的 ~60 m 节律。** MTM 前三峰 57.16 m、61.36 m、53.78 m（稳健 AR(1) ρ=0.43，点态均超 95%），另有 270/238 m 的低频能量。谱峰落在预先声明的 48–80 m 带内而**不在其中心**，说明它并非纯粹由选带造成；但选带来自 Kent & Olsen (1999) 的区域先验，仍属探索性候选。

**2. 速率搜索没有得到统计支持。** COCO 最佳 7 cm/kyr（Spearman ρ=0.378），但 **21 个速率的 rate-global p 全部 ≥0.95**；19 个 AR(1) 替代序列的最大相关为 0.369–0.450，观测值正落在其中间。7 cm/kyr 处仅 **6/9** 个目标周期可分辨（全九周期解需 ≥9.66 cm/kyr）。eCOCO 逐窗 global p 最低 0.05（仅 600–900 m），1200–1500 m 全部为 1，且不跨窗校正。**因此短偏心率检验未获证实**；19 次模拟本身也不可能达到 p<0.05。

**3. 沿剖面速率并非常数。** eCOCO 追踪速率自 300 m 的 6 cm/kyr 单调升至 1600 m 的 13 cm/kyr（294 个有限格点，0 个未解点）；定年隐含的 35 段速率为 7.6–17.1 cm/kyr。两条独立途径在"变速率"上一致，但绝对值系统性偏差约一倍。

**4. 循环计数对相位选择稳健。** 峰分支与谷分支各自独立选出 **35 个极值**，均覆盖 0–13 770 kyr。这是本方案中最实质的可靠性证据——计数不依赖"峰或谷"约定。
